blocks.text: Capacitors are used in many household appliances, such as electric fans, water pumps, washing machines, refrigerators, flashguns, computer keyboards and touchscreens.

A capacitor is connected to the starting of fan motor. When the power is turned ON the capacitor starts charging, i.e., it accumulates charge. During the process of starting of fan motor, it provides additional power, helping the motor to overcome static friction and initial resistance due to inertia. In this way, it enables the fan motor to start and begin spinning quickly. The same role is played by the capacitor in motors used in washing machines, electric blenders, choppers, grinders, water drawing motors etc.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book says the capacitor provides additional power to start the motor. It does not supply extra power or energy: it shifts the phase of the current in the starting coil relative to the running coil, so that the two coils produce a rotating magnetic field, which gives the motor its starting torque.

blocks.alt: Wiring of a fan motor. Supply terminals N and L. From the common point on N, the running coil (an outer ring of coils) goes round to L; the starting coil (an inner ring of coils) goes from the common point through a capacitor to L. Labels: Common, Capacitor, Starting Coil, Running Coil.

blocks.text: The compressors of refrigerators and air conditioners usually use single-phase motors, which can struggle to start on their own, so capacitors of high capacitance are used. Such a 'start capacitor' acts like a jump start for the compressor motor, getting it rotating; once the motor reaches a certain speed, a relay disconnects it. Most refrigerators and air conditioners also have a 'run capacitor' that stays connected to improve energy efficiency, though some older models use only start capacitors. Capacitors with resistors also form time-delay circuits, used in refrigerators, air conditioners and other devices to delay switching on the power, which protects them from power fluctuations.

In a flashgun, a capacitor stores and releases electrical energy to power the flash tube, which contains xenon gas. The capacitor is charged from the camera's battery. When the shutter button is pressed, the capacitor is connected to the flash tube, and its rapid discharge provides the high current needed to ionise the xenon, which gives a burst of bright light.

Capacitors are widely used in rectification, converting alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC); a full-wave rectifier called a bridge circuit is a typical example, and rectifiers are studied in the next chapter. In medicine, capacitors store the electrical energy needed to deliver a life-saving shock to the heart to restore a normal rhythm after cardiac arrest. They are also used in imaging machines (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound) to filter out noise and improve image clarity, and they filter out unwanted signals in EEG and ECG machines.
